utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, to everyone in the courtroom. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Madam Registrar. I was informed that you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, did some work on the transcript of yesterday and the day before, and that you had no time yet to just write down what exactly it was. If you would take that effort so that on the basis of the small note you'll then provide to the Chamber, that we'll be in a position during the break to check and to find the spots so that we can pay proper attention to what bothers you in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I asked the Registry if I could address the Trial Chamber for five minutes, or even less, for three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's about this -- if it's about the transcript issues, the Chamber would like to receive places, texts, et cetera, where there is mistranslation, so that we can check it and not spend time on it not being in a position to check it. If it's something different, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it's similar but it's also different. I would appreciate it if you could have faith in us. But during the break, I will try to give you the references, the references, the ones that we gave you yesterday. And I'd like to say -- I'd like to say this now, with your permission, because we'll waste time if you permit me to do so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think we must be in a position to check and to verify, and we can't do that on the spot. So we'll wait for the first break, and then we'll receive your short note.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President. But this is what I want to say, but I wasted a lot of time, a lot of time I wasn't able to use for the Defence of my client. But there were errors in the transcript, and this IS time I have wasted. But the Defence's rights have been violated because we cannot constantly be asked to verify things in the transcript. This is time that we have wasted, and this is time that we can't use for the defence of our client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's not time that is wasted. If there is error in the transcript, that is because making a transcript is a difficult task which cannot be made without errors, and everyone in this courtroom, Defence, Prosecution, Chamber, will do their utmost best, and it will take some time now and then to make sure that these inevitable errors will not cause any prejudice to any party. That is how the Chamber would define the situation. Yes, this is not a moment to open a discussion on it. I have expressed the view of the Chamber after you have expressed your view on the issue. Then the second thing I'd like to say: The parties are invited -- I think I gave a few examples already when Ms. Mahindaratne made objections a couple of times, that parties should limit themselves in objecting to questions to substantial issues, and not on minor issues that finally do not affect the substance of the testimony so that the flow of evidence can continue and will not be unnecessarily interrupted. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. DP5.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Ierace: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Yesterday, my last question to you concerned where the tank was kept, the tank of your armoured company. And you explained it was kept in the compound of the Nedzarici barracks, in the last facility, about 30 to 40 metres from the faculty of theology. Are the Nedzarici barracks a short distance southwest of the school for the blind on Stupska Brdo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's, if you look at it from Alipasino Polje, I think from the southwest perhaps, it's about 300 to 350 metres from the school for the blind, from the school for blind children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the tank usually kept inside a building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From where would the tank fire its rounds? Where was it when it fired rounds? Did it change its position, or was it normally in the same place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had to change its position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it always stay within the barracks, or did it sometimes leave the barracks to fire rounds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had to leave the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it go all over Nedzarici to fire rounds, or would it stay in particular parts of Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It couldn't go all over Nedzarici because the streets are very small. There are private houses there. It could only use that main road. We never used a tank to fire at residential buildings up there. It was only used down here from the barracks where there were five or six hangars in which there was nothing before the war. It was the territory of the Muslim -- of the Muslim army, and it was only built after -- there was no room for maneuvering with a tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the main road," do you mean Aleja Bosne Srebrene Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm thinking of the Aleja Branka Bujica. I don't know what that street is called now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were there mortars kept at the barracks as well as the tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you receive information about the targets for the tank? Were the targets given by the names of buildings or map references or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said we didn't fire the buildings. The tank was only used in area near the barracks because the demarcation line was by the barrack's fence. We were by the barracks, and the Muslims army was behind where there were large concrete constructions. And when the army from our positions observed where the enemy was firing from, then we would call for someone to neutralise that fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would make that call for neutralising fire? Were they the local commanders in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, since the area was not very large, it was a small lodge, and the phones were used. Old military phones were used, and they would call people from the line directly, the people who were in danger because of the enemy fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier "we didn't fire buildings." Did you, apart from the Oslobodjenje building, fire a tank at any stage at buildings, that is, positions, military positions, of the enemy in buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we couldn't have done so because the tank would have had to go right in front of our lines, and it would have been a very easy target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there not lines of sight from areas in the middle of Nedzarici to high-rise buildings surrounding Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I answer that question? Can I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there were, where the primary Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. school was, but all the routes leading to the primary school -- well only -- well vehicles could barely get to it. Perhaps a van could reach it, but a tank would have reached it with difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, an objection, but in order to -- no objection, Mr. President. But could the witness speak a little more slowly so that I can verify whether the English transcript corresponds to what he is saying in his mother tongue, which is the Serbian language. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you speak not too quickly. I would say, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that if the transcribers can follow, that would be the right speed. And I'm, for reasons of time, I think it's not appropriate to ask the witness to speak slower. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were called upon to assist other troops in Nedzarici with the tank, I take it that the tank would fire at physical objects, be they buildings or something else. Can you tell us what type of targets you hit with the tank, apart from the Oslobodjenje building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we fired from the tank -- only from the Aleja Branka Bujica because that's the road it was able to use. This happened on two occasions. Oslobodjenje was fired at on two occasions with two shells on each occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please stop. What I'm asking you is this: Do you remember yesterday you told us that the tank was used to fire some shells, to shoot some shells, at the Oslobodjenje building, and that was in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second half of June, yes. With two shells. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you did that in order to eliminate some sniper positions in that building. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you use the tank to eliminate sniper positions in other buildings at any stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use the tank to eliminate troop positions in other buildings at any stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I was explaining. Not in the buildings; only along the demarcation line, the one that ran by the barracks because that's the only place where there was room for manoeuvre and you could see enemy trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you fire at the trenches or did you fire at barricades or trees or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We fired at the trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So a tank was used to fire at trenches. Is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only at one of the front lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What else did you fire at, apart from the Oslobodjenje building and the trench or trenches at one of the front lines? What else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nowhere else, nothing else from the tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive orders to fire at targets in the city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that would have been impossible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive orders to fire at any target outside Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Nedzarici was surrounded by high buildings. It was entirely surrounded, and it was impossible for us to see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, yesterday -- I'll withdraw that. After the Oslobodjenje building collapsed, did it continue to be used by the ABiH for sniping; that is, amongst the ruins of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was no longer possible for them to climb up to the middle part where the lift was, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about from the ruins in the lower levels? Were those areas used by snipers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the building used after it collapsed -- I'll withdraw that. At the time that the building was shelled, was it used to produce the daily newspaper in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't able to know that. We couldn't see civilians moving around that building, not at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You simply didn't know. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear from any sources that the newspaper continued to be produced throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never heard that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were quite simply in hell. We didn't have electricity, and we didn't have any water. We were unable to follow --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard it since, that it was produced on a daily basis, on a regular basis, throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection because the witness is being asked what he found out after -- well, I don't know after how much time, but after the events concerned, so this objection concerns the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It goes to credibility, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The Prosecution's explanation is very brief. Why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not going to discuss in the presence of the witness the subject of the last -- the basis Mr. Ierace has laid for his response to your objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom for one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just while that's being done, to save time, could Madam Registrar please get ready to show to the witness Exhibit D1674. And secondly, could we have access to the videotape so that we could provide it to the audiovisual room and have it put at the appropriate position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the videotape in the technical room?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you wanted to expand on -- Mr. Ierace has told us that he wants to ask this question in order to test the credibility of the witness. You said it was a short explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I don't know if that is the only explanation that Mr. Ierace has, but if it's his only explanation, I don't see what could be inferred from the fact that perhaps ten years after the events, a witness discovered something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, as I understand it in the area, it's a well-known fact that throughout the war, the newspaper didn't miss an issue. And after the building collapsed, the staff continued to produce the newspaper from the ground level beneath the ruins. And that meant, of course, that civilians were travelling to that part of the city which is immediately adjacent to the area where this witness says he was operating from. The particular relevance of the question is if he says that he's never heard that, and later in the fullness of the evidence of the trial it emerges that that's incredible, that that's unlikely then that will assist the Trial Chamber in forming a view of the credibility of the witness on issues such as those. Thank you..

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As Mr. Ierace has developed this argument, I'd like to respond to it. When Mr. Ierace says that everyone in the area was aware of this, everyone in the area was aware of this on the Muslim side perhaps. This witness just said that they knew nothing about it, that it was hell, they had no electricity, they had no Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. water either. It's obvious they didn't know what was happening in the ruins of the building. If the witness said that at the time of the events he didn't know, then he didn't know at the time of the events. And to find out -- to know whether he had found this out later on has nothing to do with the credibility of the witness. It's possible to know things five or six years later but not to have known them at the time of the events. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please bring in the witness. The objection is denied, although it's not a subject that should be explored in full detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard it since that the newspaper was issued regularly throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the signing of the Dayton agreement, I went to Novi Sad. I worked in a friend's restaurant. After I returned, I found out about this, that they worked in the Oslobodjenje building. But in what capacity, how, and who, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the witness be shown D1764, and perhaps Mr. Usher could move the ELMO slightly so that I could see the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please look at the map alongside you. And with the pointer alongside your glass of water, could you please point to the position on the map, if you see it, of the barracks at Nedzarici that you've told us about where the tank was kept.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The barracks is here, so this part here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the record, the witness points to an area to the southeast of the dark black line in the vicinity -- in an area that is between the dark black line and the road marked on the map as Aleja Bosne Srebrene Street, commencing just above the circle placed on the map. It has a number in it which I can't read on the video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please place the pointer back on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And would you also point to the faculty of theology.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Witness indicates the faculty of theology which appears on the map with a circle around it. The are of the barracks is on the other side of Aleja Bosne Srebrene Street, between that street and the thick black line slightly to the north. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the main road that you told us about that the tank would travel on, would you please point to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates the road indicated on the map as Aleja Bosne Srebrene Street. Thank you, that might be returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever go into the buildings at the faculty of theology?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that there are four buildings that form that complex?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's one building. It has got four corners, and there's a park in the middle. It's a square, in fact. Only part of it, at the lower part towards Igman, there's only that part there. But it's like a square.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Given that you refer to it as one building, did that building have a ground level, and then three levels above the ground level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the building, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go, during the war, to the top of that building, that is, to the roof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to the top level of the building, that is, immediately under the roof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps on a couple of occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you ever see any snipers in that building, that is, soldiers with rifles shooting at targets outside Nedzarici, targets on the other side of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Considering that I knew the situation in Nedzarici very well, we did not have any sniper weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by a "sniper weapon"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anything which has an optical sight on it. A hunting rifle can also be a sniping weapon -- a sniper weapon, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were there ever snipers, to your knowledge, that came into Nedzarici to operate on that territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the war, nobody came to Nedzarici, not to assist us. Only people who came from Zenica. They were fleeing Zenica via Kiseljak, and they were positioned there as ordinary soldiers. They were going to the trench. But for anyone to come and help us, assist us, to be there for ten days, a fortnight, a month, to be in the trench, to be with us, to assist us, that didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did those people come from Zenica? What month, what year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly the dates. It was in 1992 because the Muslim soldiers forced us -- forced them out of Zenica, and then they would pay a thousand Deutschmarks to be let through. And then the Croats made them also pay money, and then they would come to our area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the question was as to the date, not the circumstances. And if you don't know the month, do you know the year that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in 1992. It was the beginning of the war, because they were fleeing Zenica with their families, with their wives and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you don't know the answer to this, please say so. Was Nedzarici, I suggest to you, was a particularly sensitive part of the confrontation line around Sarajevo from the perspective of the Bosnian Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, what do you mean "sensitive"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I mean by that is it was a particularly vulnerable part of the line for Bosnian Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were surrounded. Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you tell us that at no stage during the war did you receive the assistance of outside forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I state this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us what you regard as a sniper rifle, a rifle that has a scope. Were there soldiers of the Bosnian Serb army in Nedzarici who, with rifles, positioned themselves so that they could see areas on the other side of the confrontation lines? Firstly, was that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're telling us that there were not Bosnian Serb soldiers who positioned themselves with rifles so that they could see areas on the other side of the confrontation lines. Is that correct? That didn't happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lines that were established in 1992, people went to those lines, and they stood guard. Where they were, there was no movement during the war. We only lost one part of the territory in Nedzarici during the war because we couldn't stand sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps you misunderstand the question. I'll come back to that. You told us yesterday that the tank that fired on the school for the blind where your brother was, was firing from Brijesce Brdo. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you know that, where it was firing from? Did someone see it firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that my brother had told me this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you any idea how your brother knew that? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he was on that position, on one occasion, they saw when they were not being targeted, where there was a large fire, flash of fire, which came out of a barrel of a tank. That came out, and they also saw the traces of the caterpillar wheels in the soil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you where he was exactly at the school for the blind when he saw that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ground floor, ground floor, which is in the middle of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What weaponry did you see at the school for the blind when you went there during the war? Apart from pistols, what else did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Automatic rifles, only with the fold-up butts, and one hand-held rocket launcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that you did not go upstairs into any of the buildings at the school for the blind during the war. You said the reason you didn't do that was that you couldn't do that because there was a broken-glass partition where the steps were. So if you went up the steps, you could be seen from Vojnicko Polje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do not remember -- I do not recall that in the testimony of the witness we spoke of glass partition, but I can check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's my recollection that the witness said so. So please check before, and try to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. No, he did say. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember also yesterday when we saw the video, we saw some blankets being used for protection, visual blinds? And you explained that blankets and boards were used for sniper cover. Do you remember seeing that in the video yesterday, not in relation to the school for the blind but some other area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, was that area in Nedzarici somewhere, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was in Nedzarici, in the street where my house is. And it's not on the very first front line. It's about 120 metres from the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, why could that not have been done at the school for the blind to give protection to soldiers going up the stairs to the top floors of the buildings? Why could they have not erected a blanket or some wood so that they could not be seen from Vojnicko Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that they had made premises for accommodation on the ground floor of the building. There were several bunkers outside of the house, so there was no need for them to go upstairs. I don't know what the effect would have been because even they would be hit -- they were hit on the ground floor with sniper bullets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me make sure I understand what you're saying. So it's not a question of they were incapable of going upstairs, but rather they didn't need to go upstairs for defence purposes. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the army could only come across ground. We were defending ourselves from attacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it not have been better to defend yourselves from attacks if you had a safe position above ground level, so close to the front line and at such a prominent, extended point of the front line?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is a question which is completely speculative, and we're going to ask the witness whether he's got competencies of a strategist if he can answer such questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, putting to one side the inappropriateness of saying that in presence of the witness and within the hearing of the witness, this is of such basic, fundamental, and I might say an obvious nature, that one does not need any particular qualifications as a strategist to respond to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question to you. Would it not have been -- before I repeat the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please prepare to be shown to the witness shortly Exhibit P3279 OA, photograph ending with the number 3. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll repeat the question to you. Would it not have been better from the point of view of defending yourselves from attacks if you had a safe position above ground level so close to the front line and at such a prominent extended point of the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say it was unnecessary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I said, and I answered this question before, that we were at risk from the ground. They could only come from the ground. The soldiers could come across ground because it was on the ground that the trenches were, the enemy trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you had greater height, you could see more into the trenches, could you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These were extremely deep trenches, well over the height of a man. And bunkers are bunkers, and you know what they are like. They are like dams. More or less they were -- they served in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you had greater height, you could see further than you could from the ground, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you had greater height, you could perhaps see over barricades, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know because --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I don't know that. Personally, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally don't know, I take it, because as you tell us you never went up there to find out. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness now be shown Exhibit P3279 OA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While that's being prepared, how many buildings were there in the school for the blind? Just one or more than one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Look at the photograph to your right, do you see those three buildings? If, so please point to them with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates the building within the circle of the two circles, the one on the right. The circles being in the top left-hand corner of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness points to the building in the second circle which is immediately to the left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the second building. And this is the third building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness points to the building to the right of the two circled buildings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, perhaps I do not see it well on my screen, but it seems to me that the first two buildings the witness pointed at were both within one circle containing a number 1 in it, rather than in two circles.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, I see. The image on my screen could be either of those, and I accept that it's one inside the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. larger circle. In fact, I know it's the second circle, but beneath the larger circle with the one. So correct the transcript, the first two buildings indicated by the witness were both within a circle with the number one in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see a building with a circle around it and I think a number 2 in that circle? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that there is a circle with a number 2, but I can't clearly see what it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you look towards the top of the photograph, to the right of the three buildings we see a green area, perhaps a field. Is that correct? Perhaps you could point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were sport fields of the institute for blind children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just behind the field, we can see what appears to be a line of trees. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this here, in the distance?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a line of trees. These are orchard fruit trees around houses, ordinary apple trees. It's not a line of trees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That orchard, was that on the Bosnian Serb army side of the confrontation line in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. On this photograph, do you see the old people's home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Old people's home is here, about here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you actually see any of the buildings on the photograph of the old people's home, any of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photograph is very unclear. I think the old people's home is here, right here. Because next to it I see a house of a friend of mine, and I can see that his house is clear. The old people's home is a lot bigger, and it should be about there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. As you look at the photograph, was the old people's home to the left of your friend's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, for the transcript, the witness pointed at the extreme top left corner of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Immediately --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And talked about the old people's home.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, I asked you a question about where the video we saw yesterday might have been filmed from. And you said perhaps it could have been filmed from the old people's home. Having regard to the high-rise building we see in front of the old people's home as one looks at the photograph, do you agree with me that it's most unlikely the video -- the part of the video which showed the student hostels was filmed from that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I repeat, it's possible, and I'm sure that it's possible to photograph it. It looks here as if it's not there, the old people's home, as if it doesn't exist on this photograph. It's also a building with three floors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Coming back to the orchard, were there buildings behind the orchard as you look at the photograph, although we cannot see the buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were private houses, individuals houses, up to the height of two storeys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were those houses on the Bosnian Serb army side of the confrontation line during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were on our side, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the video that we saw yesterday, do you agree that all of it was taken from somewhere on the Bosnian Serb army side of the confrontation lines in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the entire video recording, everything that we saw?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What I mean is that the camera was positioned at various places in Nedzarici during the filming. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Recordings were from different parts of Nedzarici. I can show you on the map exactly where that is. It wasn't all filmed from one place --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. But clearly it was filmed from different places, but were all of those different places somewhere in Nedzarici on territory controlled during the war by the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have some still photographs which we've produced since yesterday afternoon from the video. Perhaps they could be -- one of those at this stage could be -- I'll withdraw that. I'll leave that for a moment. Might the witness be shown Exhibit P3279 NN; in particular, two photographs ending in the numbers 09 -- excuse me -- and 11. Perhaps both those photographs could be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you please look at those two photographs side by side. Firstly, I'd like to let you know that these are photographs taken after the war ended. Drawing your attention firstly to photograph ending in number 11, would you agree that in that photograph we can see the high-rise buildings of Alipasino Polje? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Alipasino Polje, in the distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And on the right, we can see Lukavicka Cesta, that is between the intersection in the immediate foreground going off to the right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is Lukavicka Cesta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please point to that street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the road going off to the left is the main road you referred to earlier. That goes down towards Ante Babica Street. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Immediately in front of the intersection, we have the shopping centre or the -- yes, the shopping centre. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the shopping centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And do you agree with me that the camera which took this photograph appears to be somewhere in the vicinity of the school for the blind, having regard to the intersection that you've identified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This building here is very well known to me. Between the school for the blind and this building, there used to be a house before the war, and it's not there now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It appears -- it's obvious from the photograph that whenever this photograph was taken, the building there was a brand-new one. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Mr. President, I'm sorry, but we have an important point to make. The witness just showed something in the transcript on the screen, that is, and he said before the war, there was a house there. And that should be entered into the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness just pointed at a house with a red roof which appears approximately in the middle of the photograph, to the left, indicated that between that house and the school of the blind, and at that moment, he pointed away from that house in the direction of the camera point of view. So not seen from the camera, behind that house, but in front of that house. He said that between the house visible and in front of that house, in between that house and the school of the blind, there had been another house before the war. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was -- first of all, perhaps you could answer the question I asked earlier. The building which appears in the photograph with the red and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. black roof appears to be newly constructed, indeed, not even finished, at the time of the taking of the photograph. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is something I would like to say about this house, but would it be possible to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is a specific issue you'd like to deal with in private session, we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, now looking at the second photograph, you'll notice that with a telephoto lens, we have a close-up of the portion of the view above the black and red roof showing the intersection of Aleja Bosne Srebrene Street and Ante Babica Street. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to point out to you a few features of this particular photograph. I'd be grateful if you could take the pointer and point to these features as I mention them so that I can be sure that you are following them. Firstly, point to Ante Babica Street, if you could run the pointer along that street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's this street here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you see above the trees slightly to the left of the bigger of the trees, one can just make out a light post, apparently on Ante Babica Street. If you could firstly point to the trees, to the left of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Move your pointer slightly to the left of the tallest tree.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just there, do you see there what appears to be a light post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a light post, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now do you know if that light post was there during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would install these sorts of light posts in the part of Sarajevo that I used to -- that I lived in. These are new light posts. It wasn't there during the war for sure. Maybe some other light post was there, but this one wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But before the war, were there light posts of a similar height in Sarajevo, parts of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, now, move your pointer slightly to the right of that same tree. And do you see some green grass. Bring it down to the grass.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you see what appears to be a ground-level entrance to the -- one of the Alipasino Polje high-rises. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it looks like, whether it's an entrance or the area where the rubbish is left, I don't know. But perhaps it's even a shop because there is some sort of inscription above it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, we see a thickish white horizontal section, and beneath it, slightly beneath it towards the middle, we can make out what appears to be part of a wall, at least there is a whitish area on the front of the wall. Do you see that? Perhaps you could put your pointer on it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Immediately to the left of the entrance, we see a light-coloured column, vertical column, of the building with one window on each level. Would you please point to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you explain that to me, please. I don't understand where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Put the pointer back on the entrance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now move it ever so slightly to the left.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now extend it upwards, directly up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see that column which has the windows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now immediately above the entrance and immediately to the right of that column we see a wider area of the facade being of a slightly darker colour. Please point to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps the ELMO could zoom back so we can see where the witness is pointing. Thank you. And then immediately to the right of that, we see another vertical light-coloured column similar to the earlier one. Please point to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the balconies are. You mean over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the balconies, slightly to the left of the balconies, we can see a whitish edge. Move the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now leave those photographs there if you will. And at this stage can we see the video from the Oslobodjenje building through to the end of the portion which shows us the student hostels. Thank you. And then it could be stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could stop the video there, in fact. Thank you. Mr. President, at this stage I'd like to distribute some photographs, being stills taken from the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I have one colour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We object, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please explain why.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we aren't sure that this was developed from this photograph. That's the first thing. And secondly, we have already had numerous problems regarding the reproduction of material. We saw this in the case of maps. We saw that reproduced maps don't have the same references. And I wouldn't like to have an Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. extract which is made and we don't know how, an extract of material that we have given, that one continues to ask the witness technical questions. Since I see that these questions concern precisions. This procedure doesn't seem to be one that is possible to us. We can't use technical means in an unacceptable manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would first like to see the photographs before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you have been provided with a coloured copy, because I see that there's a difference between the colour and the black and white copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could assist, the only other coloured copies I have at this stage are two photocopies of that coloured print. I'm happy to provide one of those to my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There's no problem in Mr. Piletta-Zanin having a look at the -- I would say the best copy available, this one. So if Mr. Piletta-Zanin would have a look at it. And perhaps ... The Chamber will concentrate for a while on the slightly less quality so the Defence is in a position to look at the best photograph. Perhaps meanwhile, Mr. Ierace, you can explain to us how and by whom this still was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Yesterday afternoon, after court, the copy of the video that was disclosed by the Defence to the Prosecution was taken to Mr. Zoran Lesic who is an earlier witness in these proceedings. And he took the video, and with his machinery, produced these prints from various positions on the video film. I have some more to come. I received them back from Mr. Lesic late yesterday afternoon. And in due course, we'll get some more colour copies done of these and provide it to the Trial Chamber and to the Defence. Mr. President, the reason I've done this is as I mentioned to you yesterday, when you look at the video on a monitor with a VHS, it's a lot clearer than it is on the courtroom monitors. I don't know that the photographs are any quantum leap from what we see on the screen, but I think they are a little bit better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, as a matter of fact, you asked us to look at the video in a better quality than appears on our screen, and therefore you extract it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have two problems, two basic problems there. The first one is whether one can know if on the basis of one document that one party provided, whether it's possible to make a patchwork on this basis, cut it up, et cetera. And with regard to this, I think it's very dangerous to manipulate in a certain sense, in inverted commas, documents that have been provided by one of the parties. And secondly, Mr. President, is that this example demonstrates very well the fact that the forces are not equal. We would never had the material possibility of carrying out such an operation with our own documents and to present situations which are totally legible or clear to the witness. The Prosecution has means at its disposal, but this isn't a reason to permit it to edit things in such a way on the basis of our documents. The Defence could never do such a thing. And for this reason, a document is a document, and you can't just cut it up into little pieces like this, take it out of its context. And the other reason is that this was never possible for us to do. We were never able to do this with elements from the Prosecution. We used a banking system. I can put it like this, with regard to documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps Mr. Piletta-Zanin could keep his voice down or take his headphones off and whisper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until 5 minutes to 11.00. And Mr. Ierace, yes.

utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I was informed that you were able to identify the spots on which you'd like to address the Chamber. utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yes, with pleasure. But now, what I want to say is that this is page 1527 [As interpreted].

The argument about the context, the Chamber considers that the context of this photograph is still available in the tape because that is still there. The Chamber also has carefully considered the equality of arms involved and raised by the Defence. The Chamber is -- finds it very important to keep a close eye on the equality of arms, and as demonstrated yesterday, where the Defence felt that they might have no access to audiotapes, and where the Chamber tried to assist the Defence as good as it could, the Chamber is of the opinion that if at -- in a similar situation the Defence would need a still of a videotape, it always can address the Chamber and the Chamber will do whatever the Chamber can to put the Defence in the same position. And therefore, to see whether such a still can be available to the Defence as well. The objection is denied, but the Chamber thought it important to give a bit more detail the reasons why the objection was denied. You may proceed, Mr. Ierace, if the witness has been escorted into the courtroom again.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now as we look at the spaces between those walls, we see a lot of dark areas. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we appear to see vertical columns with sunlight on them towards the front, around the area of your pointer. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now take your pointer to the right in those same lower levels.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Place your pointer one level further up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And in the two cavities immediately to the left of your pointer, do you see some light-coloured areas. If so, please point to them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And place your pointer again on the last of those two areas.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Over to the left.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now take it down a level.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you see a light-coloured area there as well? Do you see that, a light-coloured area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there seems to be some sort of shield here. I don't know what. Some kind of protection, some kind of screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to suggest to you that when you watch the video again in a few minutes, what we are seeing in those squares is daylight behind the building. Do you understand what I'm inviting you to observe in the next few minutes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When the video is replayed, please also look at the same area on the other building; that is, the lower floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would ask that the booth now replay the last minute or so of the video up to the point -- withdraw that. I would ask that we now see the video from the point of Oslobodjenje onwards until I ask that it be paused.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could we please rewind the video to the scene where we see the Oslobodjenje building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The technicians might not know what is the Oslobodjenje building. Starting at the beginning, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From this point onwards will do. I'm sorry, Mr. President, to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now please play it forward at normal speed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Please stop there. And rewind slowly. Rewind slower -- rewind, please. Thank you. Please stop. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we're now looking at the second of the student hostels. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And beneath the horizontal white lines, we can see a dark area which includes what appears to be a street light. Do you see that, the street light? Slightly to the left of the middle of the picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the right of the street light, in the dark area, do you see a square of a lighter colour? It seems to have a slight reddish tinge to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that the colour is different. I apologise. I'm slightly colour blind. I can't distinguish between red and blue. There is something that is different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In any event, it seems to be lighter, significantly lighter in colour, whatever colour it is, to the surrounding area. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given the position of the sun we noticed earlier, one would expect that the area beneath the building could well be in shade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the lower right-hand corner. That's how it appears, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object. I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yet again, I don't think we are referring to the same building. We are speaking about the same building. The fact that there is an angle, that the sun doesn't strike it, strike the facade in the same manner perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you cannot explain about the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then, could the witness leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I first see, you say -- your objection is you say we are not talking about the same building. As far as I understand it, questions are put by Mr. Ierace about the building on the screen. Whether this is the same building as any other building we saw before is a different matter and certainly fit if you think there would be any confusion for cross-examination. But if there's any other reason why you object, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it's the same building, but it's not the same wing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, is there any misunderstanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps there's a misunderstanding, Mr. President. This is the -- if I could put it this way: The building that we saw in the photograph earlier is the building which is presently the UN field office in Sarajevo. I think that could be generally accepted. I think Ms. Pilipovic would be aware of that. Perhaps she could agree to that. In any event, the building which we now see on the screen is not that one, but its twin. It is not a wing of the same building as the earlier one. It is the same wing of the building which is in the photograph. It might assist, Mr. President, if the video could be played for the Defence to see that it's a separate building. I would have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If perhaps before the witness comes in again that this part of the video be replayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It might be easier if it's played forward slowly because we should then see the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think that's going to take us in the wrong direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well forward is what I would usually refer to as backwards. Mr. Ierace, if you say to the left or to the right, it will certainly create no confusion, more to the left, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, it depends on where the camera is moving. So if it's played backwards, that might give us a view to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could it be played backwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Stop there, please. It should now be clear that the building on the left of the screen is the present UN field office. The building on the right is the twin of the earlier building. The building in the photograph is the building on the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you're putting questions to the witness in respect of the other building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So if the objection is that it's not the same building, you do agree on that; it is the other building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that clear, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for having put the question to me, Mr. President. But I'm still not quite convinced. I'm going to try and identify by using a photograph the background, but we can continue, I think, and we will see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the video could be forwarded, moved forward slowly. Further. Please stop there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I asked you whether you could see on the screen to the right of the light post a squarish shaped area which was lighter than the surrounding area. I think you said that you could. I think I then asked you whether, having regard to the position of the sun, it would be unsurprising if the lower levels of this building were partly in shade at the time this video was taken.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that this building has three wings, but as to the position of the sun ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You appreciate that in the upper levels, the shade is quite heavy in the cavities between the floors and walls. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you that the light square that I referred to earlier, to the right of the light post, and in fact is lighter in colour because we're seeing daylight, the effects of daylight, behind the building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In the foreground, we see what appears to be a piece of glass, as one might expect if the video was shot through a broken window space. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the lower right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could also be shadow caused by the sun on the building over there. It's quite easy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But you agree a possibility is it's a piece of broken glass in the corner of the window frame?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the lower part of the picture, we see what appears to be a flat-roofed building with a dark window immediately facing the camera. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the left, in the left part of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can't see where you're pointing on the screen unfortunately. But towards the bottom of the image, right at the bottom, so the bottom quarter, do you see running across the screen what appears to be a building with a flat roof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked you whether it was to the left, on the left side of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please point at the -- no, no, it's not possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not -- it extends from the left corner of the screen, certainly as far as the darker diagonal part of the image, and one can see behind the darker area that it indeed extends almost all the way to the bottom right-hand corner of the screen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you know of such a building in Nedzarici to the west, approximately the west, of the two student hostels, such a building that was there in Nedzarici during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But physically, that was outside of the territory of Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. To be clear on this, I'm not suggesting to you that the video was shot from the school for the blind. I'm not suggesting that we know where it was shot --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we no longer have -- we no longer have this on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have it again. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting to you it was taken from any particular place, because we don't know. Do you understand what I'm saying to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Having said that, and having regard to the angles of the buildings, I suggest to you it seems that the position was further to the right of the school for the blind, that is, closer to towards the Oslobodenje building. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to what? I didn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The point from where the photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems to be quite unclear when you say to the right, because it depends on what direction you look, and I take it there's confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Of course. Yes. I'm sorry. I left something out of the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the photograph I showed you earlier where you pointed out to us the three buildings of the school for the blind earlier this morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember that to the right of those buildings, you said -- and behind them, was an orchard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And behind the orchard, as one looked at the photograph, were some houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as one looked at the photograph, the orchard and where the houses would have been was to the right of the school for the blind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When you're looking from the student hall of residence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. I'm suggesting to you that the position of the video camera was somewhere to the right of the school for the blind in terms of that photograph you saw earlier this morning, and it may well have been further back. Would you think that a fair comment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regard to the photograph or the video recording?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to the video recording in terms of the position of the camera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there's one final photograph, but maybe from the interests of time, maybe I can avoid using it. Could the video proceed forward at a normal pace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Stop there. Now, for the benefit of the transcript, at this stage we're looking at the building that is the UN field office. That is the student hostel building further down the slope to the north. And the right wing of that building as one looks at the video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I draw your attention to the top floors of that wing, and we see extensive damage. Is that correct, to the facade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, just a correction. This building is still the student hall of residence, and the building to the left is the UN building. This building is not used as office space.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the video please be played forward slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please stop. I stand corrected. You're quite right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The top floors of the left wing of that building have extensive damage to the facade. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The horizontal strips which we see of a light colour, were they concrete, indeed, reinforced concrete?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's Ciporex, which is a soft material. It's only a sort of partition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking about the white horizontal stripes that we see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the horizontal rows, that's what we're talking about. The windows are above them. The windows are installed above them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that damage done by shells?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that damage done by fire from the Bosnian Serb army side of the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This part of the building does face our side. It faced our front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you that given the extent of the damage, it must have been caused by shells or rockets rather than small-arms fire. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it was caused by a hand-held rocket launcher because Ciporex is a very soft material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the video now be moved I think in a forward direction, although perhaps the Defence could assist me, to the red buildings. Is that forwards or back?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What red buildings, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The buildings of a red colour which were the subject of examination-in-chief yesterday. I'll just check my notes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was a previous part but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
