utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to help Mr. Ierace, but I haven't understood which building he's referring to, the building with the red roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It's all right. If the tape could be reversed quickly so that we can follow the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, could we take the time into account because the Prosecution has taken up a lot of time, more than the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The -- it's not easy to assess, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, due to translation issues, due to objections on both sides. And to be quite honest, the Chamber cannot at this moment make a precise account on the global account the Defence has taken more time than the Prosecution. So please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might the tape now be rewound at a faster speed than normal but with the image on the screen so I can alert the booth as to when to stop it. Please stop. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us yesterday, for the benefit of the transcript I should say, that the image we now see on the screen is the side of a high-rise building with a series of holes in that side. The colour is red with some horizontal lighter coloured stripes which appear to denote the floors of the building, and we are seeing it through a craggy black outline as if the film was shot through an opening. Now, you told us yesterday in relation to one of the holes that we see on the side of this building that it was used for sniping. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the film be rewound slowly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst that's being rewound, you also said that, as I understood it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please stop. Stop there, and go forward slowly. Go forward slowly. Please stop. Forward slower again. I'm sorry. Forward again. Thank you. All right. Please stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that the hole could have been made from within by the enemy forces so as to specifically create a hole for sniping. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the already-existing windows, the windows that are there. I think that these were the windows that the toilets had or the storage rooms, but they were the windows that the smaller rooms had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The windows you now refer to I take it are those which appear in a vertical line directly under the apex of the roof. Is that correct? We see one on each storey.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the left of that line, we see another hole approximately two storeys down from the top. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that also could have been made by a shell, couldn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so because there are two walls here. You've got a brick wall, and on the inside you have reinforced concrete.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate that. But that's not a reason as to why it wasn't a shell, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that a shell, a mortar shell, could create such a hole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about mortars. The Bosnian Serb army also had the benefit of artillery guns, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have such things, and they weren't active in the surroundings of Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we didn't have such things" do you mean the army surrounding Sarajevo, or do you mean the part that was in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was only referring to the army in Nedzarici. What happened in the surroundings, I don't know. I said we didn't have any electricity or water. We had no TV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Stop there. I said to you that the most efficient way to take out a sniper is with another sniper. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know. Snipers -- I withdraw that. You've told us that there were snipers on the enemy side operating against you from a variety of positions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I state this with certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they operating from the student hostels?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know they were operating from the Oslobodjenje building that we spoke about a lot. But as far as the student hostels are concerned, I don't know, because they didn't see our positions. I was hit with a recoilless shell from the student hostel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about whether you were injured. And in relation to the building on the screen, you've told us that snipers operated against your forces. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, given what you tell us was your vulnerable position in Nedzarici with snipers operating against you from high-rise locations on different sides, I suggest to you that the obvious way of responding to that threat was by the use of snipers on the Bosnian Serb army side. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I state with conviction that there were no snipers in Nedzarici in this part of the building that you are showing from the recording. It was facing -- for us it was not an advantageous position because you can see it below that there was a very large field. They were wounding our soldiers that we couldn't go and get during the day. It's some kind of a point of Nedzarici. It's not frontally facing Nedzarici. It is facing sideways, flankways.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, at any stage during the war, either in Nedzarici or anywhere else, did you ever see a sniper weapon on the Bosnian -- what you understood to be a weapon of the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that bricks would be removed, or at least small holes made, by the snipers operating on the Bosnian government side so that they could shoot from a protected space. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember, but that's not how I said it. I said that this was the first hole behind which you have some kind of partition wall. And on this other partition wall, you also have a smaller hole that was made. And we were facing at least 4.000 windows and holes, so we couldn't possibly know where from. And on here, we can see holes for --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we can see from this image that the camera seems to be shooting through a very rough hole. Do you agree with that? We can see the outlines of a hole through which the camera is shooting, or at least the outlines of an opening with rough edges through which the camera is filming.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that because of the shadows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the buildings on the Bosnian Serb army side which faced this particular building at this particular angle; that is, the building we see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that buildings, it houses, and mostly in that part, they only have one storey. [As interpreted]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, might the video be stopped, and at the moment I don't require the witness be shown an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us of three barriers that were erected on the street leading down to the intersection of Ante Babica Street, and the street we know as Aleja Bosne Srebrene Street. Do you remember saying that, three barriers across the road.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I said that first they had put two upper checkpoints just before the barricades before the conflict in Sarajevo started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would be grateful if you could confine your answers just to the questions that I'm asking in the interests of saving time. Did you understand the purpose of those barriers to be to protect persons on the other side from being fired at, being seen and being fired at, from your forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not for those three barricades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you understand their purpose to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already answered earlier. Those first two barricades remained from that time. They had put containers in old vehicles. And then when other barricades were erected, but the nearest one, the closest one to us, that is where a trench went through, a trench corridor, where the enemy forces went through. And just across Vojnicko Polje there were a few buildings that they occupied. And it was a visual protection for their own soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were visual protections for their own soldiers. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think you mentioned containers. If we can talk about them this way, the barrier closest to the intersection as barrier one, the barrier in the middle, barrier two; and the barrier closest to your positions, barrier three. Which of those three barriers, or which of them were containers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the barricades, there were those old barricades that remained. When they made the third barricade with a trench through which their soldiers went, we were no longer able to see what was happening there. It was completely sheltered from view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the last you saw of barrier one included a container or containers. Is that correct? Before you could no longer see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was barrier one made from when you last saw it during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only saw the barricade which was the closest one to us. You understand? Further, we could no longer see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever personally seen a barricade at position number 1 during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're speaking about barricade number 1, the closest one to our positions, then, yes. I don't know what you mean by barricade number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's call the barricade which is closest to your positions barricade number 3; the middle one, barricade number 2; and the barricade closest to the intersection, that is, the barricade furthest away from your positions, barricade number 1. Sir, during the war, did you personally ever see barricade 1? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never saw it. Is that your evidence, during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm stating this because we only saw the barricade number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, may I ask you how much time you think you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would have thought around 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of the problems for the Chamber is that bookkeeping, which is not our favorite sport, becomes so complicated because of the many, many objections where it seems that I'm not very successful in keeping the parties within certain limits as far as their objections are concerned. Would you please, until the next break, prioritise your subjects in the best possible way because the Chamber will have to consider what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, now, you never saw barrier 1. You never saw barrier 2 during the war. You only saw barrier 3. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you already; when the conflicts broke out, you were able to see number 1 and number 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You already told us that you never saw --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness was in the middle of answering the question. He was interrupted. This is not normal, and I believe that he is interrupted in a relatively aggressive manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I agree with you that the Chamber doesn't like any raising of voices which it hears sometimes. May I ask you now, because your last answer might have caused confusion where you were stopped halfway. We have three barriers. The closest to Ante Babica Street, close to the intersection. The one closest to your positions. And the one in between. During the war, you told us that you've seen the barrier closest to your positions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said at the very beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, at the very beginning of the war. Then the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was possible to see it, but it was just at the very beginning of the war, barricade number 1. Closest to the Ante Babica intersection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, you now called that ... I'm asking - please forget about the numbers for the time - closest to your positions, you've seen that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. After three months of war, that's the only one, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The middle one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When they made the barricade which was the closest one to us, we were no longer to see anything else. Do you understand? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say in the beginning, you might have seen the middle one, but as soon as the barricade closest to our position was erected, then we could not see the middle one any more. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the one close to the intersection with the Ante Babica Road, have you ever seen that ever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said at the very beginning of the war, yes, because that was the first one that was erected. It was the first one that was erected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For how long did you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps for two months, from the beginning of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you describe it? Did it consist of sheets, of containers, of whatever? Could you describe how the barrier was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, from the containers, made of containers, and old vehicles. It was a physical obstacle so you couldn't get through, physical barrier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, containers and old vehicles.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And then -- and it was made in this way, so that when they were doing the checkpoints on the first barricades, so that you would have to slow down. You couldn't go directly, but if you went with a car you would have to slow down and go next to it. The first one and the second. The third one was straight. And as I said, at the beginning, that they were even putting some parts of wardrobes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I've got an answer to my questions. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The building that you told us, or the house that was alongside that appeared -- I'll withdraw that. Earlier I showed you two photographs, one being a telephoto shot taken from the same position as the other, and you told us that the building which appeared in the foreground was not there during the war. There had been another building. How high was that earlier building? In this way, was it just a ground floor or was it a ground floor with more levels on top of the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the building that can be seen clearly on the photograph that I was pointing at?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were pointing at the building, and you said between that building with a red, black roof, and the Institute of the Blind, there had been another building before the war. Mr. Ierace is asking you how high was that building that is not there any more on the photograph? How high was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think two storeys. A ground floor and a storey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the witness be shown map P1785.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It was shown to the witness yesterday by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us that there was a cannon more or less at the point which appears on this map marked with the number 23. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see this cannon in that position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you show us on the map where you were when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the top of the barracks because it was snowing. For a very long time we looking where the fire was from. We couldn't find out because there was a road that was made in the hill. They had also cut through a part of the hill. And then by the road, they put a camouflage net.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was where you were when you saw the cannon. You're explaining a lot of things, but could you please concentrate very much on the question; answer that, yes. So where you were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say at the top of the barracks, how many floors up were you? Ground plus how many floors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ground floor plus two storeys. And I didn't say I was on the top. I said I was in the barracks, in the upper part of the barrack because the barrack has more than one building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that the cannon was in that position more or less, was it in the street or in a building or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained earlier. There was a part of the road that was cut through next to the road. You could see it clearly in the binoculars. The soldiers were billeted in the house just near the hill where it had been cut through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean it was in a hole in the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already explained. As the road has been cut through in a hill, the inside of the road next to the hill has been cut in so that you put the cannon there. You understand?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like the witness to be shown now a CD photograph which is P3279 E. And perhaps the witness's monitor could be put on computer evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, computer evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In a moment you will see on your screen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please give it to the -- I take it that it will be steered by your case manager.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, it will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a moment you will see on your screen a photograph which we will be able to move sideways. Accept from me, because it is not in dispute, that the photograph you're about to see was taken from the point which appears on the map marked 23. Do you understand? Do you understand what I've just said to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not the place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not the place. All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we're about to move the photograph sideways 360 degrees. I want you to look at the photograph, and if you see where the cannon was, please tell me immediately and we will stop moving the photograph. All right, please stop the photograph. I think we've just done 360 degrees.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this place, you cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you recognise what appears in the photograph at the moment? And for the benefit of the transcript, we're looking down the road, that is, the road appears to be on a slope. We're looking downwards. Do you recognise the view which appears in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And do you see in the background a row -- a number of houses at the end of the road, commencing at the end of the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see in front of those houses a road which runs across the picture, appears to be an intersection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that to be Ante Babica Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what it's called here. But in any case, that's what the street which continues from Ante Babica on, and continues on to Dobrinja, takes us to Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Will you now please turn to the map alongside you. And perhaps we could have the map on the video evidence. Thank you. Do you see Ante Babica Street to the left of number 23? If you do, please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now yesterday, as I understood your evidence, you said that between Ante Babica Street and moving towards the two confrontation lines or green lines to the left, there were houses, and they were completely destroyed during the war. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And just at the beginning of the war, they were on our side, and later on it was held by the Muslim army. So Ante Babica Street was not a confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the two lines -- I don't know how they appear to you with colour blindness. Are you able to accurately identify the colour green?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One seems to be darker to me, and the other one lighter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The darker line, does that show the forward positions of the Bosnian Serb army during the war? Perhaps you can point to the darker line, as you see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Just there. Please stop your pointer. In that area -- please bring it further down the line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates the portion of the darker line immediately to the right of Nedzarici, slightly below and slightly above.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that accurately reflect the forward positions of the Bosnian Serb army, let's say, in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately yes, but the map is not precise. It's not a correct map. It's not a proper map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the confrontation lines or the forward positions of the Bosnian Serb army, is it correct in that part, the part you've just had your pointer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this part, we had no soldiers. Nobody had any soldiers there. It's just an ordinary meadow. It was just an empty space that we were very afraid of all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. As you move further to the left, that is, towards the institute of theology, where do you say are the first houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to the primary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, the witness indicates a point where the side of the triangle, that's the red triangle indicating the cone of fire, intersects a vertical line near a group of symbols indicating buildings which is to the left of the name "Nedzarici" that appears on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said that included a primary school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these black dots. That's the primary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see also some dots on the map to the right and slightly lower of the primary school, just below and to the left of the "N" in Nedzarici? And perhaps you could point to them. I'll withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, we're at a point to have a break. I'd first like to ask the witness to be escorted out of the courtroom. We'll have a break for 20 minutes approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, could you tell the Chamber, what other subjects, how many, and what about you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Subject to whether this witness says he was in Nedzarici in December of 1992 and early January, I wish to cross-examine him on the subject of their being widespread fire, shell fire, and small-arms fire into the city on Christmas day, or eve, 25th of December, and Serbian Orthodox Christmas day, 6th of January, as well as New Year's Eve. You may recall evidence from other witnesses that that happened. This witness says he had a tank in his company. Earlier witnesses -- some earlier witnesses said they weren't there at that time of year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. That's one subject. What else?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's one subject. He was asked questions in chief about a mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And that's now in the Defence case an issue. I wish to ask him some questions about mosques. Clarify what a mountain cannon is. I don't think that will take long. There are some questions I wish to ask him in closed court which will only take a minute or two, whether he knows certain people who have already given evidence in this trial, and that has particular relevance because of the subject of tanks having regard to what some witnesses have said about there being tanks or not tanks in Nedzarici. And that's it, Mr. President. There's one other topic which I may drop. Perhaps I could indicate whether I pursue that one at the end of the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As you might have noticed, the Chamber will consider whether and how much time will still be granted to you. I also pointed that the Chamber has great difficulties in keeping both parties within the limits of their time, both while examining the witness and when objecting against the questions of the other party.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one other issue. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, if you could do it in 30 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Very briefly, it's in relation to the evidence we're hearing now about there being a field and now houses on the Serb side of the confrontation line. I would be grateful if my learned colleagues could indicate where [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it should be redacted which is not something that is already now for the outside world. Madam Registrar, would you please prepare the redaction. I'll give you some guidance once we enter into the break. Am I correct in my understanding that next week we start with the videolink testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On Tuesday. I think it's Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On Tuesday. So we still have Monday available. Yes. We'll adjourn until 5 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm just making a note that I was promised two minutes before the break. I was promised and given to Mr. Ierace. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I made a mistake. I promised you two minutes. So we'll not adjourn, but you'll first have two minutes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much indeed, Mr. President. There is a very serious problem which is happening which is the following: When I intervene for translation purposes, and I believe we can all agree on the point that I am only do this when it is essential so that everyone can understand a specific example. If a witness said at Nedzarici one tank, I have to intervene if Mr. Ierace is asking questions about several tanks because then it gives a false representation. And then when the witness says that the tank was never stationed, and in the transcript it says the opposite, I have to intervene. When I'm doing this, when I'm asked to prove it, we're wasting a lot of time, but we're doing this for everyone. We do not want this to be interpreted as being something that's done on our part to do this for any diversionary purposes. It's not doing anything else. But we're trying to save time. If these objections are taken out from our side, although this is making the hearings actually shorter, I don't think this is honest. This is not correct. It is not equitable. The very last matter in relation to time: Yesterday, we saw that the Prosecution took some 40 minutes. Today, there was not much time that was taken. And we are already now at 20 minutes to 1.00. Therefore what I wish to say, Mr. President, is that when we are asking to give our time to the points which are general interest, and therefore we are doing this for the general interest, it is not correct that -- it is not fair to somehow add it to the Prosecution time so that the Prosecution uses this for their own purposes and profit from it. This is the briefest way in which I could express myself. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. We'll adjourn until 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I promised the parties some more guidance in respect of some procedural matters. The Chamber rather prefers to continue at this very moment. I'll just give you one point of what I'll say in a more coherent way at the beginning of next week, that is that objections should be limited to not more than two lines of transcript, and it is enough to refer to what kind of objection it is. That is, relevance or question asked, question answered, or hearsay. That's clear enough, and the Chamber will then decide upon the objection, and of course will first see whether there's any need in view of the testimony at this moment and any objection as raised, whether there's any need to hear the other party on it as well. The other party would not get more than two lines as well, and then a decision will be given in order to avoid that any objection is the beginning of a lengthy argument. Perhaps the parties could keep that already in mind for the next 40 minutes. Mr. Ierace, the Chamber has decided that you'll have another ten minutes, not more certainly than 12 minutes to go. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: May I start, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us there was a mosque in the aerodrome near the airport neighbourhood. Do you see that area on the -- the position of the mosque on the map in front of you, and if so, could you please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that the map is not quite precise. But it is more or less somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness indicates a position on the map to the left of the dark-green confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could put the pointer on the map again, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. It's here. And I said that these lines weren't very precise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. On the light-green line where it intersects a road which is to the right, not necessarily the same name but if one follows the road to the right, it's indicated as bulevar Branicaca Dobrinje Street. Were there any or mosques in that area; do you remember? I take it there were not.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that mosque suffer any -- I'll withdraw that. You told us that it couldn't be seen from Nedzarici. Were there any other mosques -- any mosques that could be seen from anywhere in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, where were you on the 24th and 25th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On -- at midnight on the 24th of December, 1992, that is, Christmas eve, there was the sound weaponry being fired in large quantities all around the perimeter of Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know really. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what you did on Christmas eve, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure you were in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I suggest to you that that's what happened at midnight, and that noise lasted for about 20 minutes, that is, until about 20 minutes past midnight on Christmas day. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that piece of information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the 6th of January the date on the Serbian Orthodox calendar for Christmas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you the same thing happened on Christmas eve, according to the Serbian Orthodox rites, that is, at midnight on the 5th of January, there was a similar barrage from positions of the Bosnian Serb army around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did hear that Mr. Piletta-Zanin added one word which was not translated. I did not invite you to speak so quickly that the interpreters could not translate any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters have difficulties in understanding your language, it seems.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, question of the year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not clear. Could you please assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Willingly. The Serbian booth understood it correctly. I object because we're speaking about a different year. We have to know whether it was 1992, 1993, or 1994. So my objection, in less than two lines, was objection, the question concerns the year. The issue concerns the year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm certain it could have said in such a way that everyone would have understood right away. Mr. Ierace, would you please clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you that at midnight on the 5th of January, 1992, that the same thing happened. There was a barrage coming from Bosnian Serb army positions around Sarajevo of fire into the city that lasted some 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it, Mr. Ierace, that you're mistaken and that you are referring to the 5th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please make clear to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- whether it is a different building. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you recognise the building in the photograph? Is it one of the two buildings that corresponds to what we call the students' city? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you confirm that the upper part of this building right above, the structure above, is it white or is it light colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the top, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The following question, Witness: Could you now answer a question that is going to be purely hypothetical, purely hypothetical. Let's imagine, let's imagine that the windows of one of these buildings, it doesn't matter which one, and the inside walls disappeared because of the war. And my question is as follows: Given the angle of the -- of fire that is necessary in order to attain a point which is on the other side of the Ante Babica Avenue, that concrete floors of the building, would they have constituted an obstacle to a direct shot from the Serbian positions, regardless of where these positions were?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object. The question says it doesn't matter which building; it does. The question doesn't differentiate between the floors. There are clearly differences between the upper floors --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Question is unclear, I do understand. You're making a lot of assumptions that could all influence the answer. Would you please be more precise, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let's imagine, let's take both buildings, and let's imagine that there were no windows and no inside walls in either of the buildings. It's a hypothesis. From the Serbian positions, could a shot, a direct shot, if it were to hit a point on the other side of the Ante Babica Avenue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has already -- I hesitate to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's put the question to the witness. I think -- please continue, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do object to the question. It's difficult to do so in the presence of the witness but --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin is allowed to finish this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going to continue. For both these buildings, Witness, hypothetically, let's say there are no more windows and there are no more inside walls. So far are you with me? Do you understand the hypothesis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In this hypothesis, and I'm going to ask you the following question: From the Serb positions that you know, the presence of the horizontal floors, would it have constituted an obstacle to a direct shot? Yes or no. What I mean is to hit the Ante Babica Avenue which is located behind these buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would have constituted a problem, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very briefly, could you tell us why? Why would it have been a problem very briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we were in a far lower position, lower than these buildings, subordinate to this building. So we practically only saw the ceilings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that was a closed session matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please make a redaction, Madam Registrar. It's 92.15 until 18. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, could we go back to the question that we spoke of, the cannon. Do you remember 360-degree photograph? At the moment, I don't have the time because I haven't been given enough time to play this photograph again. But this cannon, was it stationed near - and I mean near - to what was shown on this 360-degree photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object. Inappropriate question. Leading. The evidence has given clear evidence about this, and this question does not clarify any existing misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not agree that the answer is that clear. The witness has testified you could not see the position of the tank. Could you give us any other indication on where the tank was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we are not talking about a tank. I'm sorry, we're talking about a cannon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Cannon, yes. I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. I was going to answer. The cannon was located -- what was filmed was at the bottom of the Mojmilo hill, and the cannon was at the top. So it was at the end of the regarding that we saw. It was at a much higher elevation than the position on the recording.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is approximately from where the picture was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 200, 250 metres approximately, going up Mojmilo hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you next time ask the witness in examination-in-chief what the distance was, not whether it was near or not. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following question, Witness: You said earlier that you did not receive any outside assistance, outside aid in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You meant as far as your company was concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, there is nothing in the cross-examination which requires clarification in relation to that part of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, what's the relevance, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure that I understood. You want me to say it in two words in response? Is that it? I was listening to the Serb booth, so I didn't hear what you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, indeed, Mr. President. It is important in respect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the importance. It is the issue whether it was raised in cross-examination first, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Yes, the question of outside help was raised during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Please put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please answer, Witness. Therefore, you said during cross-examination that you did not receive any outside help. To which company were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was thinking about the entire battalion in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to continue, regarding the question Oslobodjenje. You said during the cross-examination the way that this building had fallen and why it had fallen. You used the words "alone, on its own, it collapsed, alone, first wing and then another wing." You were ready to make a drawing. We don't have time for a drawing. But could you please explain to us how did this collapse happen exactly with precision, so that we know, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both parts that had collapsed were linked to the central part that can be seen. So they didn't start from the ground. First the left wing had fallen, and then three days later, right wing had fallen. The way that -- the construction of the building worked, they were attached to the central part. And only the central part had the base and the rest was like hanging. For five floors, there was nothing, and then there were these wings of the building began which later collapsed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm just is going to come -- going to come back to the question of assistance, and that will be my penultimate question. This assistance, you spoke of help in a general way, or was this specific assistance in weapons or anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, we didn't get any assistance in anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to ask you the very last question. It's with respect to the cannon on the Mojmilo side that we spoke about. When such a weapon is positioned, does it have a crew that's loading it? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As a general rule, according to normal army rules that you know, this crew, do they have to stay in position near the piece, near the weapon or on the weapon, on the piece?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How many people would have to constitute a crew for such a weapon, such a piece?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three men, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How were the supplies coming to the opposing side for this piece?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Judge Nieto-Navia has a question for you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We would like you to have a look again on the map 1785. Now, you can take a red pen and put a mark on the place where you saw a cannon. Do you remember? You talk about the water reservoir. Just put an X or something like that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reservoir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Of the position of the cannon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I respectfully intervene to point out that I think this is actually an exhibit of a Prosecution witness rather than a copy of it. I don't know whether you want to place the mark --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: The one that I have is D1785.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I don't know whether this is the one that I am talking about, but this is a Defence exhibit, not a Prosecutor exhibit. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: My question is just to put an X in the place where the cannon was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, I've already said that the map is very imprecise. It was approximately here, where this point is. Perhaps a little further up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Just put an X there, and the letter "T," as in Tom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. No more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi has no questions for you. I have got one question for you, and that is about sniping or snipers. It's not quite clear to me, was it your testimony that there were no snipers at your side, well let's say, in Nedzarici, that you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said there were no sniper weapons at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No sniper weapons. But were there -- you said a sniper weapon is with an optical sight on it, and you said a hunting rifle could even be a sniping rifle. Was there any weapon with which you would target at relatively long-distance persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We heard testimony in this Court of a witness who was on your side of the conflict that every company -- let me just find the exact words. Yes. I'll quote his exact words. He said: "Each company has to have a sniper." That was not --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was not true in the area where you ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, I knew the situation throughout the line in Nedzarici. And my information is that there was absolutely no weapons with optical sights, with scopes. No hunting rifles or any other rifles with scopes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I did put the question to you, then, in a different way. Apart from optical sights, was there any targeting of persons at a relatively long distance even if it would be without a telescopic sight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was with great difficulty that we were able to observe the people. I said we were in a lower position. On several occasions, one guard position was not just looking in front of itself, but the guard position was looking at that first one because -- to prevent the injuring, so that people wouldn't be hit through the hole that you were watching through. For instance, people were observing by watching through the rear mirror of a lorry so that you see what's happening behind you because if they were to shoot, then you wouldn't be hit. So we were observing with a system of, say, of mirrors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not quite clear to me. Could you please ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because all of our positions were only on the ground level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, only on the ground level. There were 10 or 15 cases that a person would be injured through the place that he was looking through, even if it's a very small hole. So later on, for instance, if I was in a guard position, I would be looking at the space in front of another person's guard position, and he was looking at the space in front of me. We were not looking at places in front ourselves because that's how we avoided from being hit. Or if you understand, with a rear mirror, we would be looking in the mirror to see the back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was about targeting persons at a relatively long distance, and you are telling me about how you had to protect yourself from being shot. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Yes and no. We were not able to see at a great distance from Nedzarici. We would only open fire in case of being attacked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then my last question: The weapons you had, what was approximately the killing range as far as you know? And then I'm talking about rifles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Automatic rifle, I really don't know what its killing range is. What it can go up to. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's of no use targeting targets that are outside the range, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I think that you cannot see as much with the naked eye, as much as a rifle can hit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At what distance would you target, for example, a person or a vehicle with the rifles you had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you choose a target, would you say if it's further away than 50 metres I would not even try because there's no chance to hit the target in such a way that it would cause the result I would like to achieve? Or would you say not over 200 metres or not over -- I mean, what was the distance you thought it of any use to target either persons or objects with the weapon you had, weapons you had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Considering my sight, it would be about 80 to 100 metres because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please finish your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because everyone who served in the Yugoslav People's Army, we had exercises in targeting and shooting for 50 metres. That was the outer limit, 50 metres. Before the war, that's what an ordinary soldier would hit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for your answers. This concludes your testimony in this Court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and to testify. You've answered a lot of questions from both parties, and from the Bench. And I'd like to thank you for that. And I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I just say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want to thank the Chamber for allowing me to testify. And in order just to tell you how it was, every morning, at every dawn, a new day of hell began for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is aware that living in the war circumstances has been extremely difficult for many citizens of Sarajevo. We adjourn until next Monday. I think we're still in this same courtroom, Madam Registrar, on Monday. And we only on Tuesday start the -- and I think we are sitting in the morning, I think, if I'm -- or do I make a mistake? We're sitting at the time indicated on the court calendar, next morning in this courtroom. I wish everyone a pleasant weekend. We're adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 11th day of November, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.51 p.m.,
